title: France – Passenger cars – Locations de véhicules de tourisme et utilitaire, en courte durée et moyenne durée pour le groupe RATP
description: La présente consultation a pour objet la mise en place d’un accord-cadre à bons de commandes, mono-attributaire, sans montant minimum et un montant maximum de 5 000 000 €HT, pour des prestations de locations de véhicules de tourisme et utilitaires en courte et moyenne durées. L’accord cadre est conclu pour une durée maximale de Quarante-Huit (48) mois. La démarche s’applique à l’ensemble des divisions et Business Units de l’EPIC (Etablissement Public à caractère Industriel et Commercial) et les filiales de la Ratp. Le périmètre géographique des prises de location est limité au territoire français (métropolitain), avec de possibles usages transfrontaliers. Les prestations sont définis par des locations courte durée (LCD) et moyenne durée (LMD) de véhicules particuliers et utilitaires sans chauffeur au profit des entités bénéficiaires du Groupe RATP. Les prestations concernent notamment : • Une offre professionnelle portant sur la mise à disposition de véhicules particuliers et utilitaires, • Une offre dite Loisirs, à destination des salariés du Groupe pour leurs besoins personnels. Les principales prestations attendues sont les suivantes : • Prestations de locations de véhicules de tourisme et utilitaire en courte et moyenne durée, • Mise à disposition d'un outil de réservation en ligne / site dédié pour les locations à titre personnel, • Mise à disposition des tarifs négociés dans l'outil de réservation en ligne de l'agence de voyages de la RATP, • Information, conseil et assistance auprès des différents utilisateurs du groupe RATP tout au long de la prestation de location. Pour les besoins du présent marché, la location courte durée (LCD) correspond à une durée inférieure ou égale à 30 jours calendaires consécutifs. La location moyenne durée (LMD) correspond à une durée comprise entre 31 jours et 12 mois. Afin de répondre aux différents besoins des bénéficiaires du marché, le titulaire devra proposer des offres accessibles au moyen de plusieurs canaux de réservation distincts : - Via l’agence de voyage désignée par le groupe RATP - Via une plateforme de réservation dédiée aux professionnels - Via une interface dédiée pour l’offre dite « Loisirs » Pour chacun de ces canaux, le titulaire décrira précisément les modalités d’accès, de réservation, de modification et d’annulation, ainsi que les conditions tarifaires, les moyens de paiement, les règles de validation et les prestations associées. Le titulaire veillera à assurer une présentation claire et cohérente des catégories de véhicules disponibles. Les correspondances entre les catégories commerciales proposées sur chaque canal et la classification ACRISS/SIPP devront être précisées dans son offre. À titre indicatif, le nombre de jour de location annuel est estimé à environ 33 620 et les dépenses en location de courte et moyenne durées sur l’année 2025 sont réparties entre véhicules utilitaires pour 55% et véhicules particuliers pour 45%, environ. La répartition estimée des dépenses par canal de réservation est la suivante : - Via l’agence de voyage désignée par le groupe RATP : 20 % du volume de dépenses en location de courte et moyenne durée sur l’année 2025, - Via une plateforme de réservation dédiée aux professionnels : 80 % du volume de dépenses en location de courte et moyenne durée sur l’année 2025. Cette évaluation est donnée à titre indicative et pourra évoluer en fonction des circonstances conjoncturelles du marché et ne constitue pas un engagement ferme de commande de la part du groupe RATP.

title: Z2DA--523A4-CSI-288 3.0T MRI Site Prep - Design Build West Roxbury VA Medical Center (VAMC_ West Roxbury, MA
description: Page 1 of 1 INTRODUCTION: The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Veterans Health Administration (VHA), Program Contracting Activity Central (PCAC) anticipates soliciting proposals and subsequently awarding a single Firm-Fixed-Price contract for the design-build (DB) project #523A4-CSI-288 West Roxbury VA Medical Center located in West Roxbury, MA. PROJECT DESCRIPTION: The proposed project will be a competitive, firm-fixed-price contract utilizing the design-build approach. The anticipated solicitation will be issued as a Request for Proposal (RFP) in accordance with FAR Parts 36 and 15, considering Technical and Price Factors. This project requires comprehensive design-build services for the the 3T MRI Site Preparation Design Build project at the West Roxbury VA Medical Center (VAMC) located in West Roxbury, MA. This project will provide construction of a temporary mobile Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) suite as well as all utility services and finishes necessary in the designated locations to allow for the installation of an MRI system by the Equipment Contractor. The work shall include, but not limited to, all labor, transportation, materials, apparatus, tools, equipment and permits necessary to provide for the renovation of the rooms, removal of the existing equipment, flooring, ceiling, sinks, casework, doors, shielding and installation of new flooring, ceiling, casework, doors, sinks, lighting, painting, med gas, shielding divider and relocation of electrical and HVAC work. Work to be performed at VAMC West Roxbury in accordance with the Statement of Work, Specifications, Drawings, Federal, State, and Local Codes. Strict noise and infection control measures shall be always followed. Off-hours and weekend work may be required to complete contractual requirements due to the location and sensitivity of the patient population. Existing life safety systems within Building 1 shall not be impaired at any time during the performance of the work. ADMINISTRATIVE: The anticipated solicitation will be issued as an RFP in accordance with FAR Part 36.3 Two Phase Design Build Selection Procedures and FAR Part 15 Contracting by Negotiation. The solicitation will be advertised as an SDVOSB set-aside. The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 236220 with a size standard of $45 million. The solicitation is anticipated to be issued in early November 2026. The period of performance is approximately 430 calendar days from the issuance of the Notice to Proceed. In accordance with VAAR 836.204, the magnitude of construction is between $2,000,000.00 and $5,000,000.00. This notice is not a request for competitive offers. All questions must be submitted in writing to the issuing office via email to the CS and CO: Dawn.Schydzik@va.gov and William.Henkel@VA.gov . Telephone calls will not be accepted. -END-

title: Gate Valve Frame Replacement
description: The purpose of this requirement is to replace two (2) rusted vertical frame pieces and one (1) horizontal brace of the original gate valve assembly. Work requires temporarily removing an existing electric motor-driven actuator and retained top headrail, unbolting the frame from its primary lower concrete headwall connection, field-drilling bolt holes to align and secure the retained headrail to the new vertical components, and reattaching the reassembled structure to the concrete headwall strictly in accordance with original gate manufacturer specifications. Following reinstallation of the headrail and motor actuator, the Contractor shall verify that the gate valve is fully operational, traveling freely and without obstruction between the fully open position and achieving a proper seal upon complete closure. The contractor shall provide all logistics, labor, tools, and the lawful disposal of all materials and removed components IAW Attachment 1, Statement of Work, Dated 01 Sep 2026.

description: Issue Date: 12 November 2026 Closing Date: 27 November 2026 - 2:00 PM ET This notification is connected to previous synopsis and solicitation N0016423RWS68. The work identified is to be provided by means of a Base Support, Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract with non-recurring work. Source Selection procedures will be used to evaluate and select the proposal that provides the lowest price and is technically acceptable to the Government. Offerors will be evaluated using the Lowest Prices Technically Acceptable (LPTA) Method. In order to permit efficient competition, the Navy will utilize the following methodology: Proposals will initially be screened for price and placed in order of price (lowest price to highest price). The Navy will then evaluate the non-price factors of the lowest priced proposal. The Navy will award to the Lowest Priced Technically Acceptable proposal. However, if the lowest priced proposal is not found to be technically acceptable, the Navy, at its sole discretion, reserves the right to increase the number of proposals it will review, until the Government identifies a technically acceptable proposal. Accordingly, under this methodology, the non-price factors of some proposals may not be evaluated by the Navy. If discussions are deemed necessary by the Contracting Officer, all proposals will be evaluated (both non-price and price) for the purpose of establishing a competitive range. The solicitation and resulting contract award will be a performance-based service acquisition made to the responsible offeror whose proposal, conforming to the Request for Proposals (RFP), will be advantageous to the Government price and other evaluation factors considered. NOTE: Offerors MUST be evaluated as technically ACCEPTABLE under Factors 1, 2, 3 and 4 in order to be considered technically acceptable overall. description: ********** SOURCES SOUGHT TECHNICAL DESCRIPTION AND MARKET SURVEY FOR LARGE-SCALE CIVIL WORKS CONSTRUCTION ********** ********** INTRODUCTION ********** ********** The United States Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Chicago District is issuing this sources sought synopsis as a means of conducting market research to identify parties having an interest in and the resources to support the requirement for Thomas J O Brien Lock and Dam Major Rehabilitation - Construction, Chicago, Cook County, Illinois. The intention is to procure these construction services on a competitive basis. ********** ********** BASED ON THE RESPONSES TO THIS SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE/MARKET SURVEY, THIS REQUIREMENT MAY BE SET-ASIDE FOR SMALL BUSINESSES (IN FULL OR IN PART) OR PROCURED THROUGH FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION. All Small Business Set-Aside categories will be considered. Telephone inquiries will not be accepted or acknowledged, and no feedback or evaluations will be provided to companies regarding their submissions. ********** ********** The contract type is anticipated to be Firm Fixed Price construction contract, using FAR Part 15 solicitation procedures. The proposed contract is subject to Construction Wage Rate Requirements. ********** ********** North American Industry Classification System Code (NAICS): 237990 - Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction (Size Standard: $45.0M) ********** Product Service Code (PSC): Z2KA - Repair or Alteration of Dams / Navigation Structures ********** Duration of Performance: Estimated at Three (3) Years; 1,095 calendar days. Specifics regarding the number of option periods will be provided in the solicitation. ********** Place of Performance: Thomas J O Brien Lock and Dam Major Rehabilitation - Construction, Chicago, Cook County, Illinois ********** ********** DISCLAIMER: THIS SOURCES SOUGHT IS FOR INFORMATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL (RFP) TO BE SUBMITTED. IT DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A SOLICITATION AND SHALL NOT BE CONSTRUED AS A COMMITMENT BY THE GOVERNMENT. RESPONSES WILL NOT BE RETURNED TO THE RESPONDER. NOT RESPONDING TO THIS NOTICE DOES NOT PRECLUDE PARTICIPATION IN ANY FUTURE REQUEST FOR QUOTE (RFQ) OR INVITATION FOR BID (IFB) OR RFP, IF ANY ISSUED. IF A SOLICITATION IS RELEASED, IT WILL BE SYNOPSIZED ON THE GOVERNMENT-WIDE POINT OF ENTRY (GPE). IT IS THE RESPONSIBILITY OF POTENTIAL OFFERORS TO MONITOR THE GPE FOR ADDITIONAL INFORMATION PERTAINING TO THIS REQUIREMENT. ********** ********** PROGRAM BACKGROUND ********** ********** The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Chicago District (LRC), is preparing an acquisition strategy for Phase 2 construction of the T.J. O Brien Lock and Controlling Works Major Rehabilitation project on the Calumet River in Chicago, Cook County, Illinois. The facility features a 110 ft by 1,000 ft lock chamber with concrete-capped circular sheet pile cells and low-lift sector gates regulating water exchange between Lake Michigan and the inland waterway network. As the requiring activity, USACE Chicago District delivers comprehensive engineering, design, and construction management to execute structural, mechanical, and electrical revitalization, ensuring long-term operational reliability and structural integrity. ********** ********** REQUIRED CAPABILITIES ********** ********** The scope of this requirement includes: ********** ********** *Repair and strengthening of the upper and lower guide walls and chamber lock walls through grout injection. ***Repair of a portion of the upper guide wall that was impacted by a barge in early 2026. ***Replacement of the existing sector gate operating machinery with modern equipment Revisions to the sump pump pits under the control houses for ease of maintenance ***Replacement of site hatches and covers, removal of unused pits, and rehabilitation of associated concrete and drains ***Replacement of the culvert valve gates and actuators ***Installation of two new jib cranes to service all four screens for gate openings on the controlling works ***Replacement of all gates and actuators at the controlling works ***Various upgrades to the electrical service, ductbank, and control systems associated with the items previously listed ***Upgrades to the emergency lighting and circuitry in the lock house and maintenance garage ***Upgrades to the backup generator and uninterruptible power supplies ***Revisions to the main lock house roof drain outfall to eliminate backups into the lock house when the lock water near the outlet freezes during cold weather. ********** ********** SPECIAL REQUIREMENTS AND MARKET INQUIRIES: ********** ********** Business Section ********** ********** Section A - CORPORATE CAPACITY and BONDING ********** ********** If your organization has the potential capacity to perform these contract services, please provide the following information: ********** ********** 1. Please submit a formal letter of bondability from your surety specifying your single-project limit, aggregate limit, and remaining uncommitted capacity. If utilizing a Joint Venture or teaming arrangement to meet bonding and financial underwriting requirements, detail the administrative structure and combined capacity. ********** ********** 2. Please note that under a Small-Business Set-Aside, in accordance with FAR 52.219-14 (Limitations on Subcontracting), the small business prime must perform at least 15% of the work themselves in terms of the cost of performance, excluding materials. Please provide your tailored capability statements addressing the particulars of this effort, with appropriate documentation supporting claims of organizational and staff capability. If significant subcontracting or teaming is anticipated in order to deliver technical capability, organizations should address the administrative and management structure of such arrangements. ********** ********** 3. Small Business Subcontracting: Should this requirement be solicited as Full and Open Competition, other-than-small-business offerors will be required to submit an acceptable Small Business Subcontracting Plan in accordance with RFO 19.109 and 52.219-9, as applicable. ********** ********** Interested firms are requested to describe their experience meeting small business subcontracting goals on comparable construction projects, identify potential subcontracting opportunities for small businesses, and provide preliminary estimated subcontracting percentages by socioeconomic category. Firms should also identify anticipated challenges and strategies to maximize small business participation. ********** ********** 4. Provide a comprehensive company profile including current small/large business status and socioeconomic ownership status (Small, Small Disadvantaged, Women-Owned, HUBZone, or Service Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business Concern), company profile to include number of employees, annual revenue history, office locations, UEI number, etc. ********** ********** 5. description: THE INTENT OF THIS SOURCES SOUGHT IS TO IDENTIFY QUALIFIED SMALL BUSINESSES, specifically 8(a), HUBZone, woman-owned, and service-disabled veteran-owned small businesses, for the requirement described below. The intent of this Sources Sought is to identify capable small business that can perform with limitations on subcontracting. The scope of work provides all personnel, equipment, containers, tools, materials, supervision, and other items or services necessary to perform de-manufacturing (DEMAN) operations. The Contractor shall meet the standards including disposal and recycling as defined in this Performance Work Statement for Defense Logistics Agency Disposition Services (DLA DS) site located at Gimcheon, South Korea. DLA DS disposes of foreign excess personal property of the United States Department of War (U.S. DoW). DLA DS receives property that is no longer required for use in the DoW and decides whether the property is usable or scrap. If usable property is not needed for redistribution within the Federal U.S. Government, it may be donated to state and local U.S. Governments, sold to the public, or processed for recovery of specific metals and materials required for use by the DoW. Only material that has not been disposed of by these outlets or is determined to be scrap shall be subject to this contract. The applicable NAICS code is 236220 Commercial and Institutional Building Construction, with a small business size standard of $45 million. The estimated Magnitude of Construction, in accordance with FAR 36.204, is between $100,000 and $250,000. This requirement is anticipated to be solicited as a 100% Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) set-aside. All interested SDVOSB firms must be registered in SAM.gov and verified in the SBA Veteran Small Business Certification (VetCert) database at the time of their response to be considered. The Government does not anticipate any expansion of the existing building footprint as part of this effort. The anticipated award date of the construction contract is on or before February 12, 2027. Prospective Contractors must be registered and verified in SBA s Small Business Search and https://www.sam.gov and at time of submission of their qualifications in order to be considered for an award. NOTE: Offerors are reminded of the requirements in VAAR 852.219-10, VA Notice of Total Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business Set-Aside, and VAAR 852.219-11, VA Notice of Total Veteran-Owned Small Business Set-Aside. All firms responding to this Sources Sought Notice must clearly indicate: The percentage of contract work that will be performed with the firm s own workforce. The trades or disciplines the prime contractor will self-perform. The percentage of contract work that will be subcontracted, along with: the name, location, and type/size of business (e.g., SDVOSB, VOSB, 8(a), HUBZone, small, large) for each proposed subcontractor. This information is required to demonstrate compliance with VAAR subcontracting requirements applicable to SDVOSB set-aside construction procurements. To assure compliance with 13 CFR 125.6 and VAAR 852.219-10, respondents must demonstrate their ability to comply with the limitations on subcontracting applicable to Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) construction contracts. For general construction, including installing new flooring, new cove base, and new wall paint finishes in the approved work areas, the SDVOSB prime contractor must self-perform at least 25% of the cost of the contract, excluding the cost of materials. Respondents shall provide: The percentage of work the SDVOSB prime intends to self-perform. The specific construction disciplines or tasks the prime will self-perform. Any anticipated subcontracted work (if known), including the business size/status of subcontractors (SDVOSB, VOSB, small, large, etc.). This information is required solely for market research purposes to determine whether adequate SDVOSB competition exists to support a future set-aside determination. The work includes removal and replacement of existing flooring, replacement of cove base, and repainting of walls in the scoped spaces. The work shall be performed in a professional manner, coordinated with VA staff, and completed with minimal disruption to building operations. title: Artificial Intelligence (AI) Training for the , Technology Acquisition Center (TAC)
description: Performance Work Statement TAC Artificial Intelligence (AI) Training BACKGROUND The mission of the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Office of Procurement, Acquisition, and Logistics, Technology Acquisition Center (TAC) is to support our Nation�s Veterans by providing acquisition and logistics solutions for VA. In meeting these goals, TAC is responsible for preparing and executing quality contracts that support the Information Technology (IT) efforts and needs of its customers across VA, which enables our customers to provide best value solutions to Veterans and their families. TAC employees are forward-thinking, smart, and innovative acquisition professionals, with strong technical and leadership competencies. To continue to offer our customers customized and responsive service, maintain nimble operations, and provide expert technical support services, TAC must ensure its workforce continues to enhance and maintain knowledge and awareness across a variety of current and emerging IT technologies and trends. 2. OBJECTIVES The TAC has a requirement for Artificial Intelligence training to be delivered to its workforce. All training courses shall be �live� virtual instructor led training delivered in real-time, and not pre-recorded or self-paced. All training shall be delivered prior to the end of June 2027. No training is permitted during 4th quarter of the Fiscal Year. Training shall emphasize practical application of AI to acquisition work. 3. SPECIFIC TASKS 3.1 Training The Contractor shall provide training on the following topics: Artificial Intelligence. Training will be delivered primarily to General Schedule (GS) series 0801 (GS-0801) General Engineering, GS-0854 Computer Engineering professionals as well as Contracting Professionals (GS-1102) who support TAC acquisition and business partners in the development and drafting of technical requirements and have expertise in one or more engineering service related to IT. Training attendees may include, but are not limited to: GS-0801 / 0854 General Engineer / Computer Engineers who support the development of the technical portions of the acquisition packages as well as the technical evaluations. GS-1102 Contract Specialists and Contracting Officers who support, write, and administer acquisition contracts for IT commodity and services in accordance with Federal law, regulation, and policy. GS-0340 Program Managers and GS-1101 General Business and Industry professionals who support Contracting and TAC business partners in management of programs and TAC organizational needs. Perquisites: None. Basic familiarity with Microsoft Word, Excel, Outlook, and Teams. No technical or coding background required. Training course attendance is estimated to be 25 students per class. The Contractor shall Provide Continuous Learning Points (CLPs) and Certificates of Completion for each training course. Contractors shall effectively utilize demos, knowledge checks, and hands-on learning activities as appropriate. The Contractor shall be responsible for coordinating with the Government POCs to release a welcome letter and virtual training invites for attendees. All deliverables shall be in a standardized format. Kick-off Meeting and Training Schedule (Deliverable 1) The Contractor shall conduct a kick-off meeting within one week of contract award with the Government POCs. The Contractor shall coordinate a final training schedule in accordance with the requirements of this Product Description for approval by the Government. DUE WITHIN 5 DAYS OF KICK-OFF MEETING Attendee Roster (Deliverable 2) The Contractor shall take attendance for each training course and provide an attendance sheet to the Government delivery POCs. The attendee roster shall include the name, email, and timestamps of the attendees. Training that is multi-day shall have attendance taken each day. DUE WITHIN 3 DAYS OF EACH TRAINING COURSE COMPLETION Continuous Learning Points (Deliverable 3) The Contractor shall coordinate with the designated Government POC for Continuous Learning Points (CLPs) approval with all awarded training. Training that extends for a working day (including lunch and breaks) shall be 8 CLPs per full day. The Contractor shall email a certificate of completion to each student within one (1) week of course completion. Certificates of Completion shall include, at a minimum, the name of the training course, training date(s), instructor, Contractor�s name, student�s name, and number of CLPs earned. DUE WITHIN 2 WEEKS OF EACH TRAINING COURSE COMPLETION Training Feedback (Deliverable 4) The Contractor shall collect training feedback from attendees upon completion of each training course. Feedback shall be provided to the Government delivery POCs within three weeks of each training course completion. Feedback information shall be organized and clearly presented. DUE WITHIN 3 WEEKS OF EACH TRAINING COURSE COMPLETION Course Handouts (Deliverable 5) The contractor shall provide the following handouts: Prompt Starter Library, Command Quick Reference, Document Workflow Cheat Sheet, and Responsible Use Checklist. DUE WITHIN 5 DAYS OF KICK-OFF MEETING Training Changes The Contractor shall accommodate student changes within 24-hours of the start of any training class session. Changes include student drop-out, student additions, and student switches. It does NOT include additional students beyond the stated student maximums. 3.2 Course Description This course gives acquisition professionals a practical, plain-language foundation in generative AI and shows them how to use the AI tools approved at VA to speed up everyday contracting work. Participants learn how these tools work and where they fail, how to write clear and repeatable prompts, which commands and phrases produce the results they want, and how to attach documents, spreadsheets, and templates so the AI can compare, summarize, extract, and draft from real source material. The course emphasizes safe use: protecting PII, PHI, source selection information, and other sensitive data, verifying every output, and keeping the human professional accountable for the final work product. 3.3 Learning Objectives By the end of the course, participants will be able to: Explain in plain language what generative AI is, what it does well, and why it can be confidently wrong. Identify the major AI providers and describe how the three VA-used platforms differ in strengths, interfaces, and data protections. Apply VA and federal requirements for appropriate use, including which data may and may not be entered into each tool. Build effective prompts using a repeatable structure (role, task, context, format, constraints, examples). Use common commands and instruction phrases (summarize, compare, extract, rewrite, redline, tabulate, and more) to get predictable results. Attach and reference documents, spreadsheets, and templates to compare files, find gaps, populate templates, and create new documents from source files. Refine outputs through follow-up prompts and verify them against authoritative sources (FAR, VAAR, solicitation, contract files). Select the right tool for a given contracting task and save reusable prompts for team use. 3.4 Handouts The contractor shall provide the following handouts in an easy to read format: Prompt Starter Library Command Quick Reference Document Workflow Cheat Sheet Responsible Use Checklist SECTION 508 COMPLIANCE NOTICE OF THE FEDERAL ACCESSIBILITY LAW AFFECTING ALL INFORMATION AND COMMUNICATION TECHNOLOGY (ICT) PROCUREMENTS (SECTION 508) On January 18, 2017, the Architectural and Transportation Barriers Compliance Board (Access Board) revised and updated, in a single rulemaking, standards for electronic and information technology developed, procured, maintained, or used by Federal agencies covered by Section 508 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973, as well as our guidelines for telecommunications equipment and customer premises equipment covered by Section 255 of the Communica

title: Solicitation: Construct Combat Rescue Helicopter Flight Simulator Facility at Moffett ANGB
description: The Contractor shall provide non-personal services, to include all plant, labor, transportation, materials, tools, equipment, appliances, and supervision necessary for the construction of a Combat Rescue Helicopter (CRH) Operational Flight Trainer (OFT) simulator facility at Moffett Air National Guard Base (ANGB), Mountain View, California. This project will provide an approximately 8,202 gross square foot building consisting of a multi-story, high bay area to house the CRH-OFT simulator, with a single-story area containing CRH mission planning, briefing and debriefing rooms, administrative areas for training and support staff, OFT maintenance and parts storage rooms, secure and non-secure telecommunication rooms, latrine facilities and mechanical, electrical and utility support rooms utilizing conventional design and construction. The building will be of permanent construction with electrical, mechanical, HVAC, plumbing, wet sprinkler fire suppression, fire detection, access control, direct digital control, and utility management. The exterior walls will be constructed with cavity wall construction including interior non-load bearing metal studs (or CMU wall backup at Simulator Bay) with gypsum board and exterior CMU veneer and metal panel. Air space and insulation to be located inside the cavity wall to meet Energy Code requirements. The primary roofing materials will be standing seam metal roofing to match other installation facilities and the perimeter sloped roof design will include a prefinished standing seam metal roof panel system over rigid insulation. The exterior walls will be constructed with cavity wall construction including interior non-load bearing metal studs (or CMU wall backup at Simulator Bay) with gypsum board and exterior CMU veneer and metal panel. Main entrance doors will be a pair of anodized aluminum storefront entrance doors with insulating glass including a sidelight. The Mechanical, Electrical, Sim Bay and secondary egress doors will be painted, insulated hollow metal door and frames with controlled access. Antiterrorism/Force Protection elements are incorporated. Supporting facilities include landscaping, utilities, pavements, storm drainage, sanitary sewer, site improvements, communications support, cybersecurity control systems, and tempest security.

description: Sources Sought Notice Sources Sought Notice Sources Sought Notice *= Required Field Sources Sought Notice THIS ANNOUNCEMENT IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL. THE GOVERNMENT IS UNDER NO OBLIGATION TO AWARD A CONTRACT AS A RESULT OF THIS ANNOUNCEMENT The Department of Veterans Affairs is conducting market research to identify qualified Construction Contractors capable of performing the full construction and renovation for Project No. 630SI3167B14 titled New York VA OIG Space - Flooring Replacement, Cove Base Replacement, and Wall Painting located at the Margaret Cochran Corbin VA Campus, 423 E 23rd St, New York, NY 10010. This requirement will be procured under FAR Part 36, Construction and Architect-Engineer Contracts, as a construction acquisition. The applicable NAICS code is 236220 Commercial and Institutional Building Construction, with a small business size standard of $45 million. The estimated Magnitude of Construction, in accordance with FAR 36.204, is between $100,000 and $250,000. This requirement is anticipated to be solicited as a 100% Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) set-aside. All interested SDVOSB firms must be registered in SAM.gov and verified in the SBA Veteran Small Business Certification (VetCert) database at the time of their response to be considered. The Government does not anticipate any expansion of the existing building footprint as part of this effort. The anticipated award date of the construction contract is on or before February 12, 2027. Prospective Contractors must be registered and verified in SBA s Small Business Search and https://www.sam.gov and at time of submission of their qualifications in order to be considered for an award. NOTE: Offerors are reminded of the requirements in VAAR 852.219-10, VA Notice of Total Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business Set-Aside, and VAAR 852.219-11, VA Notice of Total Veteran-Owned Small Business Set-Aside. For construction acquisitions, the prime contractor must perform at least 15% of the cost of the contract with its own employees (not including the cost of materials), consistent with the limitations on subcontracting. All firms responding to this Sources Sought Notice must clearly indicate: The percentage of contract work that will be performed with the firm s own workforce. The trades or disciplines the prime contractor will self-perform. The percentage of contract work that will be subcontracted, along with: the name, location, and type/size of business (e.g., SDVOSB, VOSB, 8(a), HUBZone, small, large) for each proposed subcontractor. This information is required to demonstrate compliance with VAAR subcontracting requirements applicable to SDVOSB set-aside construction procurements. To assure compliance with 13 CFR 125.6 and VAAR 852.219-10, respondents must demonstrate their ability to comply with the limitations on subcontracting applicable to Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) construction contracts. For general construction, including installing new flooring, new cove base, and new wall paint finishes in the approved work areas, the SDVOSB prime contractor must self-perform at least 25% of the cost of the contract, excluding the cost of materials. Respondents shall provide: The percentage of work the SDVOSB prime intends to self-perform. The specific construction disciplines or tasks the prime will self-perform. Any anticipated subcontracted work (if known), including the business size/status of subcontractors (SDVOSB, VOSB, small, large, etc.). This information is required solely for market research purposes to determine whether adequate SDVOSB competition exists to support a future set-aside determination. The work includes removal and replacement of existing flooring, replacement of cove base, and repainting of walls in the scoped spaces. The work shall be performed in a professional manner, coordinated with VA staff, and completed with minimal disruption to building operations. Time frame: The estimated period of performance for the full renovation of selected rooms within the New York VA OIG Space. The work includes removal and replacement of existing flooring, replacement of cove base, and repainting of walls in the scoped spaces. The work shall be performed in a professional manner, coordinated with VA staff, and completed with minimal disruption to building operations is 240 calendar days, excluding federal holidays. The contractor shall coordinate all shutdowns and work sequencing with the VA to minimize impact to ongoing canteen operations. description: ********** SOURCES SOUGHT TECHNICAL DESCRIPTION AND MARKET SURVEY FOR LARGE-SCALE CIVIL WORKS CONSTRUCTION ********** ********** INTRODUCTION ********** ********** The United States Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Chicago District is issuing this sources sought synopsis as a means of conducting market research to identify parties having an interest in and the resources to support the requirement for Thomas J O Brien Lock and Dam Major Rehabilitation - Construction, Chicago, Cook County, Illinois. title: Artificial Intelligence (AI) Training for the Technology Acquisition Center (TAC)
description: Performance Work Statement TAC Artificial Intelligence (AI) Training BACKGROUND The mission of the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Office of Procurement, Acquisition, and Logistics, Technology Acquisition Center (TAC) is to support our Nation�s Veterans by providing acquisition and logistics solutions for VA. In meeting these goals, TAC is responsible for preparing and executing quality contracts that support the Information Technology (IT) efforts and needs of its customers across VA, which enables our customers to provide best value solutions to Veterans and their families. TAC employees are forward-thinking, smart, and innovative acquisition professionals, with strong technical and leadership competencies. To continue to offer our customers customized and responsive service, maintain nimble operations, and provide expert technical support services, TAC must ensure its workforce continues to enhance and maintain knowledge and awareness across a variety of current and emerging IT technologies and trends. 2. OBJECTIVES The TAC has a requirement for Artificial Intelligence training to be delivered to its workforce. All training courses shall be �live� virtual instructor led training delivered in real-time, and not pre-recorded or self-paced. All training shall be delivered prior to the end of June 2027. No training is permitted during 4th quarter of the Fiscal Year. Training shall emphasize practical application of AI to acquisition work. 3. SPECIFIC TASKS 3.1 Training The Contractor shall provide training on the following topics: Artificial Intelligence. Training will be delivered primarily to General Schedule (GS) series 0801 (GS-0801) General Engineering, GS-0854 Computer Engineering professionals as well as Contracting Professionals (GS-1102) who support TAC acquisition and business partners in the development and drafting of technical requirements and have expertise in one or more engineering service related to IT. Training attendees may include, but are not limited to: GS-0801 / 0854 General Engineer / Computer Engineers who support the development of the technical portions of the acquisition packages as well as the technical evaluations. GS-1102 Contract Specialists and Contracting Officers who support, write, and administer acquisition contracts for IT commodity and services in accordance with Federal law, regulation, and policy. GS-0340 Program Managers and GS-1101 General Business and Industry professionals who support Contracting and TAC business partners in management of programs and TAC organizational needs. Perquisites: None. Basic familiarity with Microsoft Word, Excel, Outlook, and Teams. No technical or coding background required. Training course attendance is estimated to be 25 students per class. The Contractor shall Provide Continuous Learning Points (CLPs) and Certificates of Completion for each training course. Contractors shall effectively utilize demos, knowledge checks, and hands-on learning activities as appropriate. The Contractor shall be responsible for coordinating with the Government POCs to release a welcome letter and virtual training invites for attendees. All deliverables shall be in a standardized format. Kick-off Meeting and Training Schedule (Deliverable 1) The Contractor shall conduct a kick-off meeting within one week of contract award with the Government POCs. The Contractor shall coordinate a final training schedule in accordance with the requirements of this Product Description for approval by the Government. DUE WITHIN 5 DAYS OF KICK-OFF MEETING Attendee Roster (Deliverable 2) The Contractor shall take attendance for each training course and provide an attendance sheet to the Government delivery POCs. The attendee roster shall include the name, email, and timestamps of the attendees. Training that is multi-day shall have attendance taken each day. DUE WITHIN 3 DAYS OF EACH TRAINING COURSE COMPLETION Continuous Learning Points (Deliverable 3) The Contractor shall coordinate with the designated Government POC for Continuous Learning Points (CLPs) approval with all awarded training. Training that extends for a working day (including lunch and breaks) shall be 8 CLPs per full day. The Contractor shall email a certificate of completion to each student within one (1) week of course completion. Certificates of Completion shall include, at a minimum, the name of the training course, training date(s), instructor, Contractor�s name, student�s name, and number of CLPs earned. DUE WITHIN 2 WEEKS OF EACH TRAINING COURSE COMPLETION Training Feedback (Deliverable 4) The Contractor shall collect training feedback from attendees upon completion of each training course. Feedback shall be provided to the Government delivery POCs within three weeks of each training course completion. Feedback information shall be organized and clearly presented. DUE WITHIN 3 WEEKS OF EACH TRAINING COURSE COMPLETION Course Handouts (Deliverable 5) The contractor shall provide the following handouts: Prompt Starter Library, Command Quick Reference, Document Workflow Cheat Sheet, and Responsible Use Checklist. DUE WITHIN 5 DAYS OF KICK-OFF MEETING Training Changes The Contractor shall accommodate student changes within 24-hours of the start of any training class session. Changes include student drop-out, student additions, and student switches. It does NOT include additional students beyond the stated student maximums. 3.2 Course Description This course gives acquisition professionals a practical, plain-language foundation in generative AI and shows them how to use the AI tools approved at VA to speed up everyday contracting work. Participants learn how these tools work and where they fail, how to write clear and repeatable prompts, which commands and phrases produce the results they want, and how to attach documents, spreadsheets, and templates so the AI can compare, summarize, extract, and draft from real source material. The course emphasizes safe use: protecting PII, PHI, source selection information, and other sensitive data, verifying every output, and keeping the human professional accountable for the final work product. 3.3 Learning Objectives By the end of the course, participants will be able to: Explain in plain language what generative AI is, what it does well, and why it can be confidently wrong. Identify the major AI providers and describe how the three VA-used platforms differ in strengths, interfaces, and data protections. Apply VA and federal requirements for appropriate use, including which data may and may not be entered into each tool. Build effective prompts using a repeatable structure (role, task, context, format, constraints, examples). Use common commands and instruction phrases (summarize, compare, extract, rewrite, redline, tabulate, and more) to get predictable results. Attach and reference documents, spreadsheets, and templates to compare files, find gaps, populate templates, and create new documents from source files. Refine outputs through follow-up prompts and verify them against authoritative sources (FAR, VAAR, solicitation, contract files). Select the right tool for a given contracting task and save reusable prompts for team use. 3.4 Handouts The contractor shall provide the following handouts in an easy to read format: Prompt Starter Library Command Quick Reference Document Workflow Cheat Sheet Responsible Use Checklist SECTION 508 COMPLIANCE NOTICE OF THE FEDERAL ACCESSIBILITY LAW AFFECTING ALL INFORMATION AND COMMUNICATION TECHNOLOGY (ICT) PROCUREMENTS (SECTION 508) On January 18, 2017, the Architectural and Transportation Barriers Compliance Board (Access Board) revised and updated, in a single rulemaking, standards for electronic and information technology developed, procured, maintained, or used by Federal agencies covered by Section 508 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973, as well as our guidelines for telecommunications equipment and customer premises equipment covered by Section 255 of the Communica

title: Finland – Electricity – Sähköenergian hankinta
description: Laakson Yhteissairaala pyytää tarjoustanne sähköenergian toimittamisesta. Laakson yhteissairaala on rakennushanke. Rakennushankkeen aikana uudistetaan koko Laakson sairaala-alue ja tehdään uudisrakennuksen myös Ohkolan alueelle Mäntsälään. Rakennushankkeen tarkoituksena on rakentaa toimivat tilat psykiatristen ja somaattisten sairauksien hoitoon. Laakson yhteissairaalalla on tällä hetkellä 2 käyttöpaikkaa Helsingissä. Käyttöpaikkojen vuotuisen sähkönkulutuksen arvioidaan asettuvan noin 11 000 MWh tasolla vuoden 2027 osalta. Rakennushankkeen edetessä käyttöpaikkamäärä ja kulutus tulee kasvamaan. Vuoden 2028 kulutusarvio on noin 20 000 MWh, vuoden 2029 noin 25 000 MWh. Käyttöpaikka- ja kulutustiedot ovat arvioita, koska kyseessä on rakennushanke. Tarkemmat tiedot käydään valitun toimittajan kanssa läpi ennen sähköntoimituksen aloittamista. Pyydämme tarjoustanne Laakson yhteissairaalan puolesta sähköenergian myyntiin 1.1.2027 – 31.12.2027 olevalle toimitusjaksolle. Tarjouksen tulee sisältää myös optiot vuosille 2028 ja 2029, vuodeksi kerrallaan. Optioiden käytöstä tullaan päättämään erikseen sopimuskauden aikana. Sähköenergia toimitetaan avoimena toimituksena kantaverkkoon, toimitus kattaa kaikkien käyttöpaikkojen kaiken sähköenergian.

Sarah Poole Contract Specialist Page 4 of 4 CONTINUATION PAGE The following questions and answers were received from potential Quoters. Similar or duplicate questions were consolidated into a single question and response. Question 1 The Statement of Work defines DAILY as "Monday through Friday, including national holidays," while the General Requirements state service is performed Monday through Friday "excluding Federal holidays." Please confirm whether service is required on Federal holidays. Does the holiday exclusion apply to all daily services, including cleaning of the staffed historic lodge and emptying the five exterior trash receptacles? Please also confirm the first required performance day of the base period, given that the base-year period of performance begins Friday, January 1, 2027 (New Year s Day) (Attachment B, page 16). Answer 1 Services are required Monday through Friday, EXCLUDING Federal Holidays. No services are required on Federal Holidays. If the first day of the Period of Performance is a federal holiday, services will not be required on that day. The Statement of Work has been updated to reflect the change. See revised Statement of Work. Question 2 The General Requirements refer to a Federal holiday table "on page one." Please provide the holiday table or confirm the 11 Federal holidays apply. Answer 2 A list of Federal Holidays has been added to page one of the revised Statement of Work. Federal Holidays include: New Year s Day, Birthday of Martin Luther King Jr, President s Day, Memorial Day, Juneteenth, Fourth of July, Labor Day, Columbus Day, Veterans Day, Thanksgiving, and Christmas. Question 3 - Please confirm the make/model or size of the toilet paper, paper towel, and soap dispensers at each cemetery restroom and the Lodge, as well as the total number of each. Answer 3 There is one (1) 11x6 toilet paper roll holder in the outside restroom at Fort Harrison that uses standard two-ply toilet paper rolls and can hold two at a time. There are ten (10) other standard toilet paper holders between all other locations, to include inside the lodge at Fort Harrison, that shall use two-ply toilet paper. There are seven (7) paper towel holders across all locations. The type of paper towel rolls to be used are the kind bought for home kitchens; there are no flat paper towels used at any location. There are no commercial, refillable soap dispensers. Contractor shall provide ten (10) disposable, anti-bacterial soap bottles to be used across all locations. It is up to the Contractor whether to refill those bottles or replace them each time they are empty. There are no brand requirements for any of these products. Question 4 - For the semiannual Lodge cleaning (CLIN x007), please confirm the approximate number of windows and whether any second-story exterior windows require a lift or ladder access. Answer 4 There is a total of twenty (20) windows on the Fort Harrison lodge; twelve (12) on the first floor and eight (8) on the second floor. All windows require cleaning on the inside and outside. Paragraph A.4.1. in the SOW states that the most conventional method should be used to ensure maximum results. Question 5 Past performance: may the offeror's list of prior janitorial contracts include contracts performed by a proposed subcontractor (an SDVOSB or other small business that will do part of the work), as long as the offeror performs as required by VAAR 852.219-75? Answer 5 Past performance is not a requirement of this solicitation; only experience was requested under the technical qualifications section. Past Performance and experience are different. For the experience requirement under the technical evaluation section, experience should be that of the Prime. If the subcontractor also has experience, you may include their experience as well. Question 6 - Wage determination: please post a readable copy of the applicable wage determination, or give its number and revision. title: DLA-RFI-CT-2027-WBOS-MKTRES
description: NOVEMBER 20, 2026 - DLA is providing formal responses to a selection of critical industry questions received in response to the RFI for the Whole-of-Government (WoG) ordering platform (WBOS). These specific questions are being answered in advance to assist industry in their strategic preparations for the upcoming virtual Industry Day. Responses to additional pending inquiries will be integrated into the Industry Day briefing on December 2 or addressed via a separate, forthcoming pre-solicitation update. ATTACHMENT WITH RESPONSES IS INCLUDED BELOW. ************************************************************************* DEFENSE LOGISTICS AGENCY (DLA) TROOP SUPPORT CLOTHING AND TEXTILES DIRECTORATE � PHILADELPHIA, PA REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) & SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE Whole-of-Government Web-Based Ordering System (WBOS) & Commercial eMarketplace Platform FEDERAL MARKET RESEARCH NOTICE (FAR 15.201(e) & FAR Part 10): This Request for Information (RFI) is issued solely for market research, planning, and information-gathering purposes. It does not constitute a Request for Proposals (RFP), Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO), or an obligation on the part of the Government to acquire any products or services. The Government is seeking broad industry input on commercial capabilities, architectural options, and market readiness. Responses are strictly voluntary; the Government will not reimburse any costs associated with preparing or submitting responses to this notice. 1. Executive Summary & Purpose of Inquiry The Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) Troop Support Clothing and Textiles (C&T) Directorate is conducting market research to explore commercial software solutions, digital eMarketplace architectures, and industry best practices for deploying a next-generation Web-Based Ordering System (WBOS). DLA�s Troop Support C&T organization serves as the Federal Government�s primary enterprise manager for military clothing and textiles, working extensively with domestic industry. DLA is currently assessing the expansion of this shared-services procurement model to serve civilian Whole-of-Government (WOG) partner agencies, including the Department of the Interior (DOI), Department of Justice (DOJ), Department of Transportation (DOT), Department of State (DOS), and Department of Homeland Security (DHS). The primary objective of this RFI is to engage commercial e-commerce developers, SaaS providers, systems integrators, and domestic textile industry stakeholders. DLA seeks to understand what commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) and Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) capabilities exist today, how commercial technology can resolve complex federal supply chain and fiscal integration challenges, and what industry recommendations DLA should incorporate into its upcoming acquisition strategy. DLA is committed to adopting commercial best practices and avoiding custom development wherever commercial platforms can satisfy or be adapted to meet mission requirements. 2. Administrative Overview & Acquisition Milestones Market Research Parameter: Information & Acquisition Guidance Document Identifier: DLA-RFI-CT-2027-WBOS-MKTRES Anticipated Acquisition Approach: Commercial Solutions Opening (10 U.S.C. � 3458) / Commercial Acquisition (FAR Part 12 / Agile Authorities) Primary NAICS Code: 541512 - Computer Systems Design Services (Small Business Size Standard: $34.0M) Secondary NAICS Codes: 518210 - Data Processing, Hosting, and Related Services ($40.0M), 541519 - Other Computer Related Services ($34.0M) Product Service Code (PSC): DA01 - IT and Telecom - Business Application/Application Development Software RFI Issuance Date: Friday, October 30, 2026 Industry Questions & Clarifications Due: Friday, November 06, 2026, at 16:00 EST Government Formal Q&A Responses Posted: Friday, November 20, 2026 RFI Capability Response Deadline: Friday, November 27, 2026, at 16:00 EST Anticipated Pre-Solicitation Industry Day: December 2, 2026 (Virtual) Primary Contract Specialist: Courtney Hunter, Contract Specialist, DLA Troop Support C&T (Courtney.Hunter@dla.mil) Primary Contracting Officer: Ryan Zarkowski, Individual Protection and Commercial Solutions Division Chief, DLA Troop Support (Ryan.Zarkowski@dla.mil) Submission Channel: Electronic submission via email to Government POCs (Subject: 'WBOS RFI Response - [Company Name]') 3. Mission Needs & Strategic Challenges The contemplated capability would enable Government-approved vendors to list and maintain Government-approved catalogs; enable authorized agency personnel to purchase authorized items; apply agency-specific eligibility, entitlement/allowance, item-authorization, approval, and management-control rules; support authorized payment methods; and provide auditable transaction, fulfillment, and program-management information. To modernize uniform procurement across DoD and civilian partner agencies, any future solution must address several interrelated operational and regulatory challenges. Rather than dictating prescriptive technical designs, DLA outlines the desired functional outcomes below to invite innovative, industry-driven solutions: Operational Domain: The Operational Challenge / Desired Outcome Commercial Marketplace & User Experience: Deliver a modern, consumer-grade multi-tenant e-commerce experience with sub-second catalog search, faceted filtering, mobile responsiveness, and intuitive uniform selection, while supporting distinct tenant agency branding (DoD, DOI, DOJ, DOT, DOS, DHS) and role-based permissions. Domestic Provenance & Supply Chain Integrity: Because DLA operates as a central procurement hub utilizing the Defense Working Capital Fund (DWCF), end-items transacted through DLA are subject to 100% domestic sourcing requirements under the Berry Amendment (10 U.S.C. � 4862). DLA requires automated mechanisms to verify domestic origin down to the raw material/mill level, screen supply chains for forced labor or prohibited foreign entities, and prevent unverified items from being purchased. Statutory Competition & Micro-Purchases: In a multi-vendor marketplace environment, transactions must respect federal competition mandates (such as CICA and simplified acquisition thresholds). The Government seeks automated, user-friendly marketplace workflows that promote fair competition, facilitate dynamic quoting between micro-purchase thresholds ($15k) and simplified acquisition threshold ($350k), and prevent improper order splitting without creating administrative bottlenecks. Uniform Customization & Value-Added Logistics: Civilian law enforcement and military personnel require customized uniforms (e.g., branch tapes, badges, department patches, embroidery, reflective safety trims, and tailored sizing). The system must support interactive customization, dimensionally accurate digital proofing, supervisor approvals, and tracking of value-added tailoring services while ensuring all component materials remain compliant. Interagency Accounting & Fiscal Guardrails: The system must handle interagency funding across diverse partner departments without risking Antideficiency Act (ADA) violations. This includes integrating with federal financial frameworks (such as Treasury G-Invoicing Form 7600A/B), managing annual individual officer uniform allowances (5 U.S.C. � 5901), supporting multi-payment split tender (allowance + GPC + personal card overages), and reconciling DLA cost-recovery surcharges without contractor fee retention. Cybersecurity & Enterprise Interoperability: The platform will process sensitive federal uniform requisitions, military supply chain data, and law enforcement personnel information. It must meet high federal cybersecurity baselines (such as FedRAMP and DoD Cloud Computing Security Requirements), support CAC/PIV single sign-on, and interface with federal backbones such as DLA Enterprise Business System (EBS/SAP), PIEE/WAWF, and SAM.gov. title: Testing of USCG TRACEN Cape May Potable Water
description: This is an amendment to a solicitation for commercial services prepared in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Quotations are being requested, and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation number 67100PR270000313 is issued as a Request for Quotation (RFQ) for monthly potable-water sampling and laboratory testing services at U.S. Coast Guard (USCG) Training Center (TRACEN) Cape May, 1 Munro Avenue, Cape May, NJ 08204. This acquisition is a Total Small Business Set-Aside. The solicitation incorporates applicable provisions and clauses by reference and in full text, as identified in the attached Commercial Provisions and Clauses document. Full text of FAR provisions and clauses may be accessed electronically at https://www.acquisition.gov/. The associated North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 541380, Testing Laboratories and Services. The applicable small-business size standard is $23.5 million in annual receipts. The Product Service Code (PSC) is F103, Environmental Systems Protection�Water Quality Support. The anticipated contract type is firm-fixed-price. Offerors shall provide all-inclusive firm-fixed monthly prices for the base period and all option periods. Offerors are required to provide prices for all CLINs. A zero-dollar ($0.00) unit price means that the offeror will provide the service at no charge to the Government. Unit prices left blank or annotated with something other than a dollar figure may be considered unacceptable. SUBMISSION OF QUOTATIONS Submit quotations by email only to SMB-FORCECOM-042@uscg.mil. The email subject line shall read: �RFQ 67100PR270000313 � Testing of USCG TRACEN Cape May Potable Water � [OFFEROR NAME]� Quotations are due no later than 27 November 2026, 1600 Eastern Standard Time (EST). Quotations received after the stated closing date and time may not be considered. As a minimum, quotations shall include: (1) A cover page identifying the offeror�s legal business name, physical address, Unique Entity Identifier (UEI), CAGE code, if applicable, primary point of contact, telephone number, email address, and the name and title of the individual authorized to bind the offeror; (2) A completed pricing schedule for every CLIN, including the base period and all option periods. Prices shall be firm-fixed-price and all-inclusive; (3) A technical capability narrative demonstrating the offeror�s capability and management approach to meet all Statement of Work (SOW) requirements. At a minimum, address sampling coordination and collection procedures; chain-of-custody, preservation, transportation, and field-measurement procedures; laboratory analytical capability and ability to use the SOW-required analytical methods; timely electronic reporting and immediate-notification procedures; proposed personnel and equipment; and ability to comply with USCG facility-access, safety, identification, and security requirements; (4) Current evidence of New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection (NJDEP) laboratory certification applicable to the required testing. If the offeror will use a subcontract laboratory, identify the laboratory and provide its applicable NJDEP certification; (5) At least two, but no more than three, recent and relevant past-performance references for comparable potable-water, drinking-water, wastewater, environmental sampling, or laboratory-analysis services performed within the past five years. For each reference, provide customer name; contract or project title; brief description of work performed; dollar value; period and place of performance; customer point of contact name, title, telephone number, and email address; and a brief explanation of relevance to this requirement; and (6) Acknowledgment of all solicitation amendments and a statement identifying any exceptions to solicitation terms and conditions. Offerors shall ensure applicable entity-level representations and certifications in the System for Award Management (SAM) are current and accurate, or otherwise submit representations and certifications required by the solicitation. PERIOD FOR ACCEPTANCE OF QUOTATIONS The offeror agrees to hold the prices in its quotation firm for 60 calendar days from the date specified for receipt of quotations. DESCRIPTION OF REQUIREMENT USCG TRACEN Cape May requires a qualified contractor to provide all labor, supervision, equipment, sample containers, preservatives, transportation, laboratory analysis, and documentation necessary to conduct monthly potable-water sampling and laboratory testing. The Contractor shall collect potable-water samples from the first accessible potable-water sampling point downstream of the TRACEN Cape May water tower, or from another sampling location designated by the Government Technical Representative (GTR). Required testing includes total coliform, Escherichia coli (E. coli), free available chlorine residual, pH, turbidity, and total trihalomethanes (TTHMs). The Contractor shall use an NJDEP-certified laboratory for all required laboratory analyses. The Contractor shall coordinate each monthly sampling event with the GTR at least five business days in advance, unless otherwise agreed. The Contractor shall submit the required laboratory report and chain-of-custody documentation within 21 calendar days after sample collection. The Contractor shall notify the GTR by telephone and email within one business day after receipt of any result indicating E. coli detection or any result identified by the laboratory as requiring immediate notification or corrective action. See the attached SOW for complete requirements, including analytical methods, performance standards, contractor personnel requirements, installation-access requirements, and deliverable acceptance procedures. SITE VISIT AND INSTALLATION ACCESS No organized site visit will be conducted. Contractors must pass a background check and present a Real ID or valid driver�s license with a secondary form of ID, along with valid vehicle registration and insurance. If a contractor cannot meet these requirements, they must be escorted by a CAC holder throughout their visit, which may cause delays or denial of access if no escort is available. For questions regarding visitor access, contact the designated Government POC. SOLICITATION QUESTIONS Questions concerning this RFQ shall be submitted by email only to SMB-FORCECOM-042@uscg.mil no later than 20 November 2026, 1600 EST. Questions received after this deadline may not be answered. Oral explanations or instructions are not binding. The Government will issue material changes to this solicitation by written amendment. BASIS FOR AWARD The Government intends to make a single firm-fixed-price award to the responsible small-business offeror whose quotation conforms to the solicitation and represents the best value to the Government using comparative analysis, considering technical capability, past performance, and price. 1. Technical Capability. The Government will evaluate the extent to which the offeror demonstrates a sound and feasible approach to fulfilling the SOW, including potable-water sample collection; required analytical testing; NJDEP-certified laboratory capability; reporting; urgent-notification procedures; personnel; equipment; and compliance with installation-access requirements. 2. Past Performance. The Government will evaluate the recency, relevance, and quality of the offeror�s past performance for services similar in scope and complexity to this requirement. The Government may consider submitted references and information obtained from other reasonable sources. 3. Price. The Government will evaluate total evaluated price by adding the extended prices for the base period and all option periods. Prices will be evaluated for completeness, reasonableness, and balance. Evaluation of option prices does not obligate the Government to exercise any option. A qu

Sarah Poole Contract Specialist Page 4 of 4 CONTINUATION PAGE The following questions and answers were received from potential Quoters. Similar or duplicate questions were consolidated into a single question and response. Question 1 The Statement of Work defines DAILY as "Monday through Friday, including national holidays," while the General Requirements state service is performed Monday through Friday "excluding Federal holidays." Please confirm whether service is required on Federal holidays. Does the holiday exclusion apply to all daily services, including cleaning of the staffed historic lodge and emptying the five exterior trash receptacles? Please also confirm the first required performance day of the base period, given that the base-year period of performance begins Friday, January 1, 2027 (New Year s Day) (Attachment B, page 16). Answer 1 Services are required Monday through Friday, EXCLUDING Federal Holidays. No services are required on Federal Holidays. If the first day of the Period of Performance is a federal holiday, services will not be required on that day. The Statement of Work has been updated to reflect the change. See revised Statement of Work. Question 2 The General Requirements refer to a Federal holiday table "on page one." Please provide the holiday table or confirm the 11 Federal holidays apply. Answer 2 A list of Federal Holidays has been added to page one of the revised Statement of Work. Federal Holidays include: New Year s Day, Birthday of Martin Luther King Jr, President s Day, Memorial Day, Juneteenth, Fourth of July, Labor Day, Columbus Day, Veterans Day, Thanksgiving, and Christmas. Question 3 - Please confirm the make/model or size of the toilet paper, paper towel, and soap dispensers at each cemetery restroom and the Lodge, as well as the total number of each. Answer 3 There is one (1) 11x6 toilet paper roll holder in the outside restroom at Fort Harrison that uses standard two-ply toilet paper rolls and can hold two at a time. There are ten (10) other standard toilet paper holders between all other locations, to include inside the lodge at Fort Harrison, that shall use two-ply toilet paper. There are seven (7) paper towel holders across all locations. The type of paper towel rolls to be used are the kind bought for home kitchens; there are no flat paper towels used at any location. There are no commercial, refillable soap dispensers. Contractor shall provide ten (10) disposable, anti-bacterial soap bottles to be used across all locations. It is up to the Contractor whether to refill those bottles or replace them each time they are empty. There are no brand requirements for any of these products. Question 4 - For the semiannual Lodge cleaning (CLIN x007), please confirm the approximate number of windows and whether any second-story exterior windows require a lift or ladder access. Answer 4 There is a total of twenty (20) windows on the Fort Harrison lodge; twelve (12) on the first floor and eight (8) on the second floor. All windows require cleaning on the inside and outside. Paragraph A.4.1. in the SOW states that the most conventional method should be used to ensure maximum results. Question 5 Past performance: may the offeror's list of prior janitorial contracts include contracts performed by a proposed subcontractor (an SDVOSB or other small business that will do part of the work), as long as the offeror performs as required by VAAR 852.219-75? Answer 5 Past performance is not a requirement of this solicitation; only experience was requested under the technical qualifications section. Past Performance and experience are different. For the experience requirement under the technical evaluation section, experience should be that of the Prime. If the subcontractor also has experience, you may include their experience as well. It does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP) or an obligation on the part of the U.S. Government to contract for any supply or service whatsoever. The Government does not intend to award a contract on the basis of this synopsis alone or otherwise pay for the information requested. This can look like; more assets per beam line, faster batch cycling, additional beam lines, etc. Reducing single-point mechanical bottlenecks and optimizing robotic manipulator uptime in radiography bays, allowing for increased exposure capacity or reducing auxiliary asset logistics timelines. In addition, seeking opportunities to enable or increase uptime efficiency of low-power reactor operations and/or film exposure reductions without a drop in fidelity, and/or increasing exposure volume for additional concurrent small scale assets to extend the service life or efficient use of restricted, non-obligated research reactor core fuel.INSTRUCTION1. title: Notice of Intent to Sole Source - Modernized Airborne Radio Control Head MARCH / Control Head Unit (CHU)
description: The U.S. Army Contracting Command � Aberdeen Proving Ground (ACC-APG), on behalf of the Product Manager, Aviation Mission Systems Architecture (PM AMSA), intends to award a sole-source, five-year Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract, with a provision for a six-month extension in accordance with FAR 52.217-8, to Mercury Systems, Inc., CAGE Code 096Y5, located at 2665 Gulf Breeze Pkwy, Gulf Breeze, FL 32563. The Government projects contract award for December 2026. The Government requires the procurement of a Modernized Airborne Radio Control Head (MARCH) / Control Head Unit (CHU) solution to provide form, fit, function, and interface (F3I) cockpit radio control for the Air-to-Ground Networking Radio (AGNR) System and to replace the obsolete C-12601 Control Indicator (CI) within the AN/ARC-231A Radio Set across Army tactical rotorcraft (UH-60M/V Black Hawk, CH-47F Chinook, AH-64D/E Apache), designated fixed-wing aircraft, and unmanned aircraft systems (UAS). This effort will procure commercial-derivative Communication Management Units (CMUs), Mercury Systems ACM-9000 series hardware, specifically ACM-9544 CHUs and ACM-9443J CIs. The scope also encompasses airworthiness certification data and artifacts, proprietary operating system and runtime software licenses, and modernized MARCH engineering design, systems integration, and qualification testing services. This acquisition is being conducted on a sole-source basis under the authority of 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1), as implemented by FAR 6.302-1 and RFO 6.103-1(c)(2)(ii), which authorizes contracting other than full and open competition when there is only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements. Mercury Systems, Inc. is the original equipment manufacturer (OEM) and the sole owner of the proprietary hardware manufacturing data packages, circuit schematics, FPGA register configurations, and safety-critical software source code for the qualified ACM-9544 and ACM-9443J units. The Government does not possess licensing rights to this technical data, and any alternative vendor would require an estimated 18 to 30 months to redesign, environmentally qualify, and airworthiness certify a replacement system. A schedule slip of this duration is unacceptable as it directly conflicts with the required AGNR 3QFY27 system-level production timeline and the early 3QFY28 C-12601 delivery date, which would exhaust depot supply channels and lead to mission degradation of operational aircraft. Responses must be submitted via email no later than 4:00 PM EST on 27 November 2026 to the Contracting Officer, Roxanne Barbaris at roxanne.barbaris.civ@army.mil, and the Contract Specialist, Jessica Lefever, at jessica.d.lefever.civ@army.mil.
